title: The 10 Best Roofing Nailers
subtitle: Pneumatic and cordless coil roofing nailers for asphalt shingles, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A coil roofing nailer drives shingle nails fast and to a consistent depth, which matters for a roof that keeps water out. We ranked 10 best-sellers from BOSTITCH, Metabo HPT, DEWALT, WEN and value brands on rating, review volume and features (depth adjustment, a selectable trigger, a shingle guide, dry-fire lockout and carbide nose inserts).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.flag: A pallet and fencing nailer, not a roofer; inflated speed claim
avoid.verdict: A coil nailer built for pallets and fencing that shows up in roofing searches, with an exaggerated speed claim.
reasons: It's a CN55 coil framing nailer for pallets, crates, furniture and fences, and shoots 1 to 2-1/4 inch nails, longer than roofing nails, with no shingle guide.
It claims 'Max 12 nails per second (2 times faster than normal coil nail gun)'. Metabo HPT's pro roofer is rated up to 10 per second, and the other roofers here that list a speed say 3.
It's rated 3.8 stars on 28 reviews. The 3PLUS HCN45SP is a real roofing nailer for less.

buyers_guide.q: What nails does a roofing nailer use?
buyers_guide.a: Coil roofing nailers take 11-gauge, full-head, wire-collated 15-degree coils from 3/4 to 1-3/4 inches. Metabo HPT's model uses 16-degree coils.
The guide sets the exposure so each course lines up without measuring, which speeds up shingling and keeps rows straight.
Overdriven nails cut through shingles; underdriven nails stand proud and lift shingles. Tool-free depth adjustment lets you dial it in as conditions change.
Bump (contact) firing is fast for production roofing. Sequential is safer and more precise.
Pneumatic roofers are lighter and faster for whole roofs. Cordless suits repairs where hauling a compressor up isn't worth it.
